pass: Sky Lab galaxy rotation measurements and mass explorer
changes: Two published SPARC examples: all 43 radial samples for NGC 3198 and all 31 for NGC 6503, including speed errors, gas and stellar model terms.
Linked measured-speed and difference diagrams on fixed speed scales, selected-radius readouts and adjustable stellar mass-to-light ratio.
Discrete sample selection through a native slider, keyboard or touch; controls retain investigation notes and normalize malformed saved inputs.
Signed gas contributions and negative differences remain visible; quoted random errors are separated from model uncertainty.
Explorer appears inside the rotation-curve topic; other dark-matter topics keep their existing compact panels.
Corrected compact-mass rotation explanation and present-day versus early-universe energy-budget claims; preserved percentage-bar proportions.

scientificScope.equation: v_bar² = Vgas|Vgas| + Υ_disk Vdisk|Vdisk| + Υ_bulge Vbulge|Vbulge|
scientificScope.uncertainty: Quoted random speed errors only; no inclination systematic or model uncertainty is added.
scientificScope.assumptions: Gas, light profiles, adopted distances and inclinations remain fixed. No dark halo or modified-gravity model is fitted.
scientificScope.inference: The explorer compares a mass assumption with measurements; it does not establish a particle identity or compute a joint likelihood.

provenance.verification: Every included value is checked against the published fixed-width table columns. Content hashes normalize CRLF to LF for portable verification; original download hashes are also retained.

sources.title: SPARC 2016 galaxy properties and original rotation references
Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert 2016: SPARC mass models
sources.use: Equation 2, signed gas contributions and reference M/L

sources.title: Planck 2018 VI: Cosmological parameters
sources.use: Base ΛCDM interpretation and present-epoch density budget

limits: This is an inspection of two bundled historical SPARC examples, rather than a live catalog query.
Model segments join published radii; selection snaps to actual samples.
The scalar status compares one model value with a quoted error bar and has no formal detection significance.
Remaining particle-candidate and dark-energy topic claims were not comprehensively re-audited in this pass.
